# Combined higher-order handlers and guarded value graphs

Status: candidate research construction, pending primary elaboration and fresh
independent review. Production authority: none. Parent:
`HO-HANDLER-GRAPH-COMPOSITION-1`, paper guarded values 180–196, recursive
allocation 980–993, shallow handlers 399–456, local preservation 1069–1088,
and safety 1139–1159. The original paper theorem and Simple-sub A/B, F1/FK1
quantifiers remain OPEN.

Contract: `HANDLER-GRAPH-EXTENSION-THEORY-20261025/r1`, SHA-256
`b0b9f069dc8f08ed5f87a26b37d98df404e5a9dd4f0628244adc79095634a9e8`.
Author: `/root/handler_graph_composition_astra_r1`; primary `/root` supplied the
wait-result reference coverage reminder and cancellation-hypothesis shadowing
repair observation. Neither is eligible to independently certify this packet.
Requested model/effort: `gpt-6-astra/medium`; observed model/effort: UNKNOWN.
No descendants, additional dependencies, scratch paths, compiler changes or
production semantic decisions.

## Original claim and candidate application

The parent needs one actual syntax and execution relation supporting both
accepted languages simultaneously. Separate safety theorems were insufficient:
the old graph machine suspends requests/failures inside finite evaluation
contexts, while the old handler machine propagates them to the root. The new
candidate constructs the shared grammar, derives finite observations from the
actual graph typing and guard, and proves preservation and root-only progress
for every finite raw internal prefix. It then connects both old machines and
consumes the actual old recursive allocation supplier under an independently
typed combined handler.

`HandlerGraphSyntax` has six mutually recursive sorts: Value, Comp, Adapter,
Handler, ValueArms and OperationArms. Every accepted Graph and Handler
constructor is represented structurally. References, recursive names and local
indices remain distinct. Lambda bodies, outer result consumers, adapter input
bodies, request response binders, value-arm binders and both operation-arm
binders contain the full combined language. The existing Ty, modes, operation
instances, literal payloads and all metadata fields are reused unchanged.
Extrinsic typing and structural renaming/substitution cover every constructor.
The six cancellation lemmas justify substitution after binder insertion; they
are applied to the actual context resumption equation.

`HandlerGraphEmbedding` recursively embeds both old languages in arbitrary
typing contexts. Its renaming/substitution commutation lemmas are consumed by
actual old-step simulation. `liftGraph_typed` derives new node typing from old
node derivations. `liftGraph_projection` proves exact equality of the guard
projections, so `liftGraph_guard` transports the existing guard. Projected unit
is only a stopping token; it supplies neither typing nor a canonical value.

`HandlerGraphSafety` derives `ObservedTyped` from actual node typing and the
transparent successor rank. Intersection has two separate premises, top retains
its underlying type witness, and wrap retains different inner and outer callable
types and both adapters. No typing premise occurs in `Step`. Lookup is explicit
for force, union/intersection elimination, absurd and dynamic call, and also for
references returned as No/Yes carriers inside both kinds of wait. The machine
retains all shallow-handler trial, ordering, skipping, nesting, propagation and
restoration rules. The selected arm receives the original K:Q→A; only exhaustion
constructs the shifted handler around K, yielding H K:Q→B. Eligibility remains
raw Bool data, with no native permission adequacy claim. `preservation` assumes
actual closed graph typing; `closed_progress` additionally consumes the guard.
`finite_prefix_safety` quantifies over every raw finite internal trace.

`HandlerGraphCorrespondence.graph_step` and `handler_step` map every old raw
step, actual event and complete lambda/wrap entry plan. Their finite trace
versions preserve event order. `propagate_graph_request` and
`propagate_graph_failure` construct finite sequences through every old context;
`graph_suspended_root` consumes the old full suspension decomposition.
`graph_request_correspondence` retains the identical full operation instance and
payload and derives the resulting continuation typing from the old contextual
computation typing plus actual propagation. `graph_resume_equation` states that
substituting any combined response into the propagated continuation equals the
same outer context around the original response-substituted K.
`old_graph_resume_equation` further identifies this with the embedding of the
old resumed contextual computation. `graph_resumption_safety` applies the
supplier to arbitrary independently typed responses and every subsequent
internal prefix, without consuming the saved code or imposing linear use.

`source_rec_under_handler` calls the exact accepted `source_rec_allocation`,
lifts its actual allocated graph and closed body, derives combined typing and
guard, and establishes every finite prefix under an independently typed combined
handler. Its only fresh guard premise is the old actual `FreshNoCycle`; no new
fresh-node typing or rank supplier is introduced. `SourceExample` starts with
an empty old graph, closes a genuinely recursive source lambda with a request
and self-call in the response continuation, gives the exact allocated-node
equation, and executes its request through handler selection. `Examples` also
executes a recursive graph lambda through a graph-backed attempt/wait result,
and a nested request followed by restoration, reference lookup and Yes return.
The examples supplement the quantified statements.

## Reused evidence and exact open boundaries

The accepted Handler syntax/substitution/trial construction and Graph
syntax/allocation/observation construction are reused within their actual finite
constructor domains. Their independent safety conclusions were not assumed to
compose. The previous contextual graph terminal convention is not reused as
combined root progress. Literal readback, template replay, closure environments
and historical Call proofs are not treated as universal higher-order native
readback or metadata suppliers. No failed or withdrawn Simple-sub bypass is
restored. No residual, provider, witness or foreign-continuation lineage is
identified by this construction.

The original paper remains OPEN for omitted μ/type-changing roll,
polymorphism, mapop, primitive and other forms. This packet does not allocate
arbitrary new combined handler-valued RHS simultaneously: it embeds the actual
accepted old RHS allocation and permits independently typed combined handlers
around its body. Combined external responses carrying fresh graph extensions
remain a future integration with the independent extension lane; no cross-lane
import is assumed. Live metadata, grants, activation/owner freshening and full
source/native correspondence remain OPEN. The internal safety candidate does
not imply F1, FK1, inference soundness/principality or production adoption.

## Source/native audit and mutual TODOs

`tools/inference-playground/src/runtime/machine.rs` was inspected at these
actual owners:

- `begin_local` (2500) allocates an empty cell, extends recursive environments
  before evaluating the initializer, and pushes `Frame::Local`. The return
  branch (1498) installs the received value into that cell. The proof's immutable
  finite graph allocation is not an established readback of every such native
  execution or arbitrary initializer.
- `propagate_request` (2081) examines the installed CatchReturn delimiter,
  validates its installation, resolves declarations and demands a local Grant
  unless the closed primitive certificate applies. A Bool arm flag is not a
  proof that these live checks succeed.
- `TemplateNode::ForwardHandler` replay (1989) resolves and validates the owner,
  allocates a fresh handler occurrence, and installs CatchReturn. The finite
  syntax retains identity/metadata but proves no activation freshness or owner
  adequacy theorem.
- `Frame::CatchReturn` (1097) returns the incoming value when no value arm exists.
  The accepted paper empty value trial fails with MatchFailure. Existing
  `HO-HANDLER-VALUE-EMPTY-1` remains OPEN; no identity-arm normalization or runtime
  defect verdict is inferred.

`NO_SAFE_CODE_SLICE`: these owners need the missing source/readback and semantic
premises before any dependent production patch. No compiler edit is proposed.
The following requests specify evidence, not permission to write or run:

| Request | Owner / first missing evidence | Exact falsifier |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HG-ALLOC-READBACK-1 | Luna/native source intake; map actual begin_local/Frame::Local cells, captured environments and accepted recursive RHS code to the immutable allocation and prove all reachable supplier premises | An accepted recursive initializer/capture path has no typed graph readback, or exposes an unfilled cell along a claimed represented path |
| HG-HANDLER-METADATA-1 | Luna/metadata source intake; supply full operation-instance, Grant, installation and owner-freshening correspondence for propagate_request and ForwardHandler | A claimed represented typed execution returns HandlerEvidence or violates restored owner/activation identity despite the proposed supplier premises |
| HG-EMPTY-VALUES-1 | Existing HO-HANDLER-VALUE-EMPTY-1 owner; resolve native no-arm return versus paper MatchFailure under approved semantics | Direct mapping of an empty value-arm CatchReturn yields Ret natively and Fail formally |
| HG-EXTENSION-INTEGRATION-1 | Luna future proof intake; transport the independent extension construction through the complete six-sort grammar and saved combined waits | An old saved handler-bearing continuation loses typing or changes its old node/operation identity after an admitted fresh extension |

These requests preserve original owners and quantifiers. No local frame action
is offered as a replacement for the independently quantified foreign continuation
obligation. Primary elaboration and fresh independent review are the immediate
next steps for this candidate, before any finite-domain theorem acceptance.

All other direct/transitive frozen dependencies retain their exact contract table

design_note_text:
# Higher-order research core and structural embedding

Status: Draft research construction; checking and review evidence is recorded in
the sprint outcome and its frozen receipts. This is not production authority.
Scope: frozen LEAN-HIGHER-ORDER-PROOF-CORE-20261025/r1 research representation.
Initial author: /root/higher_order_proof_core_astra_r1; requested gpt-6-astra/medium,
observed model/effort UNKNOWN. Primary /root repairs and integrates after author
STOP; the outcome records final authorship and independent review. No descendants.
Production authority: none. The operational paper is a proposal/target; the
2026-10-07 complete-Call definition §1 records permission for legitimate research
definitions, not adoption of this representation as compiler architecture.

The parent RESPONSE-ENCODING-1 / ENV-CALLABLE-1 lacked a callable constructor in
its formal Value sort. The candidate removes that specific representational
obstruction by constructing a new callable type and actual lambda/wrap values.
Every Original.Val/Comp and TypedCall.Value/Comp/Adapter/Function constructor is
mapped structurally. No old term is retained behind an opaque original opcode.
The full parent, native readback and operational safety remain OPEN.

## Syntax and quantifiers

`HigherOrderSyntax.lean` retains every old type constructor, all eight literal
domains and their exact payload representations, variables, delay, injections,
single-child intersection/top values and all seven Original computations. It
adds the existing Call view/scope/expose/request/fail nodes, lambda/wrap values,
and dynamicCall. Request's continuation binds its operation instance's response
type. The type language can place callable types beneath thunk/union/intersection
and in operation instances. The value, computation and adapter syntax is mutually
inductive; all typing judgments are defined afterwards.

Value-entry lambda binds A; computation-entry lambda binds Thunk A. Both retain
receipt, annotated input/body/result types, body and result consumer. Wrap keeps
the input adapter c→a and output adapter b→d around an a→b function. DynamicCall
accepts a thunk carrier. This fixes a research typing interface without asserting
an execution rule or operational equivalence for the new constructor.

`ContextEmbedding old new` quantifies over every old lookup fact. The mutual
Original and TypedCall preservation proofs quantify over arbitrary old terms,
old typing derivations and target contexts satisfying that relation. Closed
Original nodes embed under any target context using the empty lookup relation;
binders use `extend_embedding`. The Function theorem quantifies over every old
FunctionTyped derivation and every target context. No original constructor,
source-domain restriction or independent continuation quantifier is discarded.
This is one-way typing preservation, not reflection or full conservativity.

## Metadata boundary

Paths retain component lists, port kinds and translated endpoint types;
occurrences retain identities and paths. Operation instances retain operation
identity, ordered type arguments and both payload/response types. Receipt slots
and profiles retain order, identity and typed paths. Adapter metadata retains
all path correspondences and captured occurrences. Interface-port metadata also
has a structural map.

PathRule is a Prop in the accepted input. `embedPathRule` translates its proof
into a new Prop proof. It does not eliminate that proof into a data-valued map
identity. In particular the old permissive adapterMap rule remains permissive;
this work cannot prove that a mappingIdentity absent from runtime data can be
reconstructed. Syntax is **typing-proof-free**, not entirely proof-free. The old
Adapter.typed field is omitted from syntax and consumed solely to construct the
new extrinsic AdapterTyped derivation. The retained PathRule metadata neither
contains a typing judgment nor creates a typing-definition cycle.

## Parent application

`embedFunction_typed` constructs a ValueTyped callable from an old FunctionTyped
proof. `function_as_argument` and `call_with_function_argument` use it in the
actual new delayed argument and dynamicCall constructors.
`request_callable_response` constructs a request that binds and returns a
callable-typed response. `function_cell` pushes the embedded function into the
existing generic NativeClosureEnvironment.Store, proves the actual current cell
equality and supplies its callable typing derivation.

`read_embedding` preserves the exact old selected cell address while mapping the
current store pointwise. `read_embedding_typed` combines that equation with the
accepted `successful_read_typed` theorem. `captured_value_typed` applies the
accepted `realized_substitution_typed` supplier to each represented context index;
`captured_body_typed` applies its actual successful capture and closed-body
construction before embedding. Both keep successful realization and CellsTyped
as explicit original premises. Nothing claims that arbitrary native closures
already satisfy those premises, or that old stores already represent new
callable values. Generic new callable storage and old represented-read transport
are two separate constructions whose native connection is still open.

## Remaining source obligations and reuse

Accepted CoreSyntax typing and CallEnvironmentRealization supply precisely their
existing domains. CoreSubstitution's bind/request lifting is reused through
close_body, without reproving lookup or assuming a new substitution rule. The
NativeClosureEnvironment.Store remains generic; no machine fields change.
Historical literal readback is not extended to callable readback by analogy.
No failure is dismissed by a narrower theorem; no new source restriction,
Simple-sub bypass or production implementation is introduced.

Luna/source intake owns ENV-LAYOUT-1 (resolved free-variable order and binder
indices from source Lambda/Name/Apply), ENV-CELL-VALUE-1 (current native Value
encoding), ENV-GRAPH-1 (recursive cell/closure graphs), ENV-CALLABLE-1's remaining
native body/consumer mapping, and ENV-DISPATCH-1. Relevant native owners remain
machine.rs `Instruction::Lambda`, `Frame::ValueEntry`, `Machine::lookup`,
`Machine::extend`, closure/Callee branches and receiving.rs lambda schema
construction. The primary's disjoint source map gives their complete exact
producer/consumer inventory, including unit/record/default entry cases.
Force, native transitions, new-core substitution/progress/preservation,
whole-trace safety, operation authenticity and original inference A/B remain
OPEN. No F1/FK1 or foreign-continuation theorem is claimed here.

## Intake and checks

No Lean/build/tests/native checks were run by the author. A shell `python`
invocation failed because the executable was absent; the generation was then
performed with python3. This was a file-writing failure before any write, not a
failed proof check. Primary owns bounded elaboration, public signature/axiom
inspection, distinguishing examples, repairs after author STOP and fresh
independent review. Author/coauthor cannot independently certify this candidate.
Only the four exact leased files were created; there are no scratch paths,
background processes, descendants, compiler changes or Git operations.

import YulangClosure.GraphExtensionTransport

/-! Actual saved graph requests through finite heterogeneous immutable extensions.
Research candidate: no native cell/store or handler correspondence is assumed. -/
namespace YulangClosure.HigherOrderGraph.Extension
open HigherOrder (Ty Context emptyContext extend OperationInstance)
open Safety
variable {R T U : Type} {xi : R → Ty} {tau : T → Ty}

structure Saved (R : Type) where
  operation : OperationInstance
  payload : Value R Empty
  continuation : Comp R Empty
  context : EvalContext R

variable {s : Saved R}

def Saved.suspended (s : Saved R) : Comp R Empty :=
  s.context.plug (.request s.operation s.payload s.continuation)

def Saved.resume (s : Saved R) (response : Value R Empty) : Comp R Empty :=
  s.context.plug (substComp (single response) s.continuation)

/-- The internal result type is existential; the full operation determines the
response binder. This predicate is derived from the actual request below. -/
def SavedTyped (xi : R → Ty) (s : Saved R) (result : Ty) : Prop :=
  ∃ bodyResult, ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext s.payload s.operation.payloadType ∧
    CompTyped xi emptyTy (extend emptyContext s.operation.responseType) s.continuation bodyResult ∧
    ContextTyped xi emptyContext s.context bodyResult result

theorem capture_typed (s : Saved R)
    (h : CompTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext s.suspended result) : SavedTyped xi s result :=
  request_context_typing s.context h

theorem saved_suspended_typed (h : SavedTyped xi s result) :
    CompTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext s.suspended result := by
  obtain ⟨b, hp, hc, hk⟩ := h
  exact plug_typed hk (.request hp hc)

/-- A real reached request supplies every saved typing premise. -/
theorem capture_reached {g : Graph R} (hg : WellTyped g xi)
    (initial : CompTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext m result)
    (steps : Steps g m trace s.suspended) : SavedTyped xi s result :=
  capture_typed s (trace_preservation hg steps initial)

theorem capture_decomposition {m : Comp R Empty}
    (h : CompTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext m result) (request : Requested m) :
    ∃ s : Saved R, m = s.suspended ∧ SavedTyped xi s result := by
  obtain ⟨k, op, payload, continuation, eq⟩ := request
  refine ⟨⟨op, payload, continuation, k⟩, eq, ?_⟩
  apply capture_typed _
  change CompTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext (k.plug (.request op payload continuation)) result
  rw [← eq]
  exact h

def Saved.map (f : R → T) (s : Saved R) : Saved T :=
  ⟨s.operation, mapValue f s.payload, mapComp f s.continuation, mapContext f s.context⟩

theorem saved_map_id (s : Saved R) : s.map id = s := by
  cases s
  simp only [Saved.map, mapValue_id, mapComp_id, mapContext_id]

theorem saved_map_comp (f : R → T) (g : T → U) (s : Saved R) :
    (s.map f).map g = s.map (fun r => g (f r)) := by
  cases s
  simp only [Saved.map, mapValue_comp, mapComp_comp, mapContext_comp]

theorem saved_map_suspended (f : R → T) (s : Saved R) :
    (s.map f).suspended = mapComp f s.suspended := by
  simp only [Saved.suspended, Saved.map, map_plug, mapComp]

theorem saved_map_resume (f : R → T) (s : Saved R) (v : Value R Empty) :
    (s.map f).resume (mapValue f v) = mapComp f (s.resume v) := by
  simp only [Saved.resume, Saved.map, map_plug, map_substitute_top]

theorem saved_map_typed (f : R → T) (types : ∀ r, tau (f r) = xi r)
    (h : SavedTyped xi s result) : SavedTyped tau (s.map f) result := by
  obtain ⟨b, hp, hc, hk⟩ := h
  exact ⟨b, mapValue_typed hp f types, mapComp_typed hc f types,
    mapContext_typed f types hk⟩

theorem saved_resume_typed (h : SavedTyped xi s result)
    (response : Value R Empty)
    (hr : ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext response s.operation.responseType) :
    CompTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext (s.resume response) result := by
  obtain ⟨b, hp, hc, hk⟩ := h
  exact plug_typed hk (substitute_top hc hr)

/-- Operation matching is full structural equality, never just the operation ID.
This raw interface rule does not assume response typing or preservation. -/
inductive Answer (s : Saved R) : OperationInstance → Value R Empty → Comp R Empty → Prop where
  | matched (operation : OperationInstance) (same : operation = s.operation) (response) :
      Answer s operation response (s.resume response)

theorem mismatched_instance_rejected (different : operation ≠ s.operation) :
    ¬ Answer s operation response next := by
  intro h
  cases h
  contradiction

theorem answer_typed (hs : SavedTyped xi s result)
    (hr : ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext response operation.responseType)
    (answer : Answer s operation response next) :
    CompTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext next result := by
  cases answer
  subst_vars
  exact saved_resume_typed hs _ hr

/-- Actual finite chains can change the reference sort at every extension.
The data contains concrete embeddings, without choosing any inhabitants. -/
inductive Chain (R : Type) (graph : Graph R) (xi : R → Ty) :
    (T : Type) → Graph T → (T → Ty) → Type 1 where
  | refl : Chain R graph xi R graph xi
  | snoc {T U : Type} {middle : Graph T} {tau : T → Ty} {last : Graph U} {ups : U → Ty} :
      Chain R graph xi T middle tau → Embedding middle tau last ups →
      Chain R graph xi U last ups

def Chain.embedding {g : Graph R} {xi : R → Ty} :
    {T : Type} → {h : Graph T} → {tau : T → Ty} →
      Chain R g xi T h tau → Embedding g xi h tau
  | _, _, _, .refl => .refl g xi
  | _, _, _, .snoc priorChain e => (Chain.embedding priorChain).trans e

theorem chain_old_nodes {g : Graph R} {h : Graph T}
    (chain : Chain R g xi T h tau) (r : R) :
    h (chain.embedding.refs r) = mapValue chain.embedding.refs (g r) :=
  chain.embedding.nodes r

theorem chain_injective {g : Graph R} {h : Graph T}
    (chain : Chain R g xi T h tau) : ∀ {r s}, chain.embedding.refs r = chain.embedding.refs s → r = s :=
  chain.embedding.injective

theorem chain_saved_typed {g : Graph R} {h : Graph T}
    (chain : Chain R g xi T h tau) (hs : SavedTyped xi s result) :
    SavedTyped tau (s.map chain.embedding.refs) result :=
  saved_map_typed _ chain.embedding.types hs

/-- Parent application for EVERY finite extension chain and EVERY new-world
response. The response can mention fresh references absent from the old graph. -/
theorem chain_resume_safety {g : Graph R} {h : Graph T}
    (chain : Chain R g xi T h tau)
    (captured : CompTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext s.suspended result)
    (finalTyped : WellTyped h tau)
    (finalGuard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph h))
    (response : Value T Empty)
    (hr : ValueTyped tau emptyTy emptyContext response s.operation.responseType)
    (steps : Steps h ((s.map chain.embedding.refs).resume response) trace last) :
    CompTyped tau emptyTy emptyContext last result ∧ CanProgress (graph := h) last :=
  finite_prefix_safety finalTyped finalGuard
    (saved_resume_typed (chain_saved_typed chain (capture_typed s captured)) response hr) steps

/-- Each response is quantified independently; the first execution does not
consume or mutate the captured record used by the second execution. -/
theorem repeated_responses {g : Graph R} {h : Graph T}
    (chain : Chain R g xi T h tau)
    (captured : CompTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext s.suspended result)
    (ht : WellTyped h tau) (guard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph h))
    (one two : Value T Empty)
    (hOne : ValueTyped tau emptyTy emptyContext one s.operation.responseType)
    (hTwo : ValueTyped tau emptyTy emptyContext two s.operation.responseType)
    (first : Steps h ((s.map chain.embedding.refs).resume one) t1 n1)
    (second : Steps h ((s.map chain.embedding.refs).resume two) t2 n2) :
    (CompTyped tau emptyTy emptyContext n1 result ∧ CanProgress (graph := h) n1) ∧
    (CompTyped tau emptyTy emptyContext n2 result ∧ CanProgress (graph := h) n2) :=
  ⟨chain_resume_safety chain captured ht guard one hOne first,
    chain_resume_safety chain captured ht guard two hTwo second⟩

/-- The identity of the OLD saved continuation after a second extension is an
actual syntactic equation, not merely equality of result types. -/
theorem saved_after_second {g : Graph R} {h : Graph T} {k : Graph U} {ups : U → Ty}
    (chain : Chain R g xi T h tau) (extension : Embedding h tau k ups) (s : Saved R) :
    (s.map chain.embedding.refs).map extension.refs =
      s.map (Chain.snoc chain extension).embedding.refs :=
  saved_map_comp _ _ s

/-- Allocation supplies final typing and guard, as well as exact immutable old
nodes. Fresh source RHS derivations and the finite cycle criterion are consumed. -/
theorem source_allocation_resume {g : Graph R} {nu : Fin n → Ty}
    (hg : WellTyped g xi) (guard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph g))
    (s : Saved R) (captured : CompTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext s.suspended result)
    (rhs : Fin n → HigherOrder.Value)
    (hrhs : ∀ i, HigherOrder.ValueTyped (sourceContext nu env) (rhs i) (nu i))
    (hcapture : CapturesTyped xi env capture)
    (hcycle : FreshNoCycle (sourceFresh capture rhs))
    (response : Value (Sum R (Fin n)) Empty)
    (hr : ValueTyped (joinTy xi nu) emptyTy emptyContext response s.operation.responseType)
    (steps : Steps (allocate g (sourceFresh capture rhs))
      ((s.map Sum.inl).resume response) trace last) :
    CompTyped (joinTy xi nu) emptyTy emptyContext last result ∧
      CanProgress (graph := allocate g (sourceFresh capture rhs)) last := by
  have ht := allocate_typed hg (sourceFresh capture rhs)
    (fun i => sourceCloseValue_typed (hrhs i) hcapture)
  have hg' := allocationGuard guard (sourceFresh capture rhs) hcycle
  exact finite_prefix_safety ht hg'
    (saved_resume_typed (saved_map_typed Sum.inl (fun _ => rfl)
      (capture_typed s captured)) response hr) steps

/-- Arbitrarily many independently chosen responses, including an empty family.
No response is required to be representable in the original reference sort. -/
theorem finite_response_family {g : Graph R} {h : Graph T}
    (chain : Chain R g xi T h tau)
    (captured : CompTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext s.suspended result)
    (ht : WellTyped h tau) (guard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph h))
    (responses : Fin count → Value T Empty)
    (typed : ∀ i, ValueTyped tau emptyTy emptyContext (responses i) s.operation.responseType) :
    ∀ i trace last, Steps h ((s.map chain.embedding.refs).resume (responses i)) trace last →
      CompTyped tau emptyTy emptyContext last result ∧ CanProgress (graph := h) last :=
  fun i _ _ steps => chain_resume_safety chain captured ht guard _ (typed i) steps

/-- Four explicit outcomes at every final prefix; graph suspension decomposes
into a request or failure in its actual finite evaluation context. -/
theorem chain_resume_four {g : Graph R} {h : Graph T}
    (chain : Chain R g xi T h tau)
    (captured : CompTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext s.suspended result)
    (ht : WellTyped h tau) (guard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph h))
    (response : Value T Empty)
    (hr : ValueTyped tau emptyTy emptyContext response s.operation.responseType)
    (steps : Steps h ((s.map chain.embedding.refs).resume response) trace last) :
    Returned last ∨ Requested last ∨ Failed last ∨ ∃ event next, Step h last event next :=
  progress_four ht guard (chain_resume_safety chain captured ht guard response hr steps).1

/-- A finite external interaction protocol over the ACTUAL graph machine.
Publication requires an actual context-decomposed request. Existing saved records
are immutable, all records transport on extension, and any stored record can be
resumed repeatedly. This is a research interface, not native scheduler authority.
Internal rules are exactly Safety.Step; external responses alone carry typing. -/
inductive Run (R : Type) (initialGraph : Graph R) (initialTypes : R → Ty)
    (initial : Comp R Empty) :
    (T : Type) → Graph T → (T → Ty) → Comp T Empty → List (Saved T) → Prop where
  | start : Run R initialGraph initialTypes initial R initialGraph initialTypes initial []
  | internal {T : Type} {g : Graph T} {tau : T → Ty}
      {current next : Comp T Empty} {event : Event T} {arena : List (Saved T)} :
      Run R initialGraph initialTypes initial T g tau current arena →
      Step g current event next →
      Run R initialGraph initialTypes initial T g tau next arena
  | publish {T : Type} {g : Graph T} {tau : T → Ty}
      {arena : List (Saved T)} (saved : Saved T) :
      Run R initialGraph initialTypes initial T g tau saved.suspended arena →
      Run R initialGraph initialTypes initial T g tau saved.suspended (saved :: arena)
  | extension {T U : Type} {g : Graph T} {tau : T → Ty} {h : Graph U} {ups : U → Ty}
      {current : Comp T Empty} {arena : List (Saved T)}
      (e : Embedding g tau h ups) :
      Run R initialGraph initialTypes initial T g tau current arena →
      WellTyped h ups →
      Run R initialGraph initialTypes initial U h ups (mapComp e.refs current)
        (arena.map (Saved.map e.refs))
  | answer {T : Type} {g : Graph T} {tau : T → Ty} {saved : Saved T}
      {current next : Comp T Empty} {arena : List (Saved T)}
      {operation : OperationInstance} {response : Value T Empty} :
      Run R initialGraph initialTypes initial T g tau current arena →
      saved ∈ arena → Answer saved operation response next →
      ValueTyped tau emptyTy emptyContext response operation.responseType →
      Run R initialGraph initialTypes initial T g tau next arena

/-- Saved-record typing is established only by actual publication, then retained
by immutable transport and reuse. No saved typing oracle is an input to Run. -/
theorem run_invariant {g : Graph R} {h : Graph T}
    (hg : WellTyped g xi) (initial : CompTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext m result)
    (run : Run R g xi m T h tau current arena) :
    WellTyped h tau ∧ CompTyped tau emptyTy emptyContext current result ∧
      ∀ s, s ∈ arena → SavedTyped tau s result := by
  induction run with
  | start =>
      refine ⟨hg, initial, ?_⟩
      intro s hs
      cases hs
  | internal prior step ih =>
      exact ⟨ih.1, preservation ih.1 step ih.2.1, ih.2.2⟩
  | publish saved prior ih =>
      refine ⟨ih.1, ih.2.1, ?_⟩
      intro s hs
      rcases List.mem_cons.mp hs with eq | old
      · subst s
        exact capture_typed saved ih.2.1
      · exact ih.2.2 s old
  | extension e prior typed ih =>
      refine ⟨typed, mapComp_typed ih.2.1 e.refs e.types, ?_⟩
      intro s hs
      obtain ⟨old, member, eq⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hs
      subst s
      exact saved_map_typed e.refs e.types (ih.2.2 old member)
  | answer prior member matched typed ih =>
      exact ⟨ih.1, answer_typed (ih.2.2 _ member) typed matched, ih.2.2⟩

/-- Parent safety induction for arbitrary finite INTERLEAVINGS of internal
steps, capture, extension and repeated responses. Every final internal prefix
and every stored old continuation retains the original overall result type. -/
theorem run_prefix_safety {g : Graph R} {h : Graph T}
    (hg : WellTyped g xi) (initial : CompTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext m result)
    (run : Run R g xi m T h tau current arena)
    (guard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph h))
    (steps : Steps h current trace last) :
    CompTyped tau emptyTy emptyContext last result ∧
      (Returned last ∨ Requested last ∨ Failed last ∨ ∃ event next, Step h last event next) ∧
      (∀ s, s ∈ arena → SavedTyped tau s result) := by
  obtain ⟨typedGraph, typedCurrent, typedArena⟩ := run_invariant hg initial run
  have typedLast := trace_preservation typedGraph steps typedCurrent
  exact ⟨typedLast, progress_four typedGraph guard typedLast, typedArena⟩

namespace Demo
abbrev unitTy : Ty := .base .unit
abbrev callableTy : Ty := .callable unitTy unitTy
def receipt : HigherOrder.ReceiptTemplate := ⟨[], []⟩
def operation : OperationInstance := ⟨73, [callableTy], unitTy, callableTy⟩
def delayedOperation : OperationInstance := ⟨74, [callableTy], unitTy, .thunk callableTy⟩
def old : Graph (Fin 1) := fun _ => .unit
def oldTypes : Fin 1 → Ty := fun _ => unitTy

theorem old_typed : WellTyped old oldTypes := fun _ => .unit

def oldGuard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph old) :=
  GuardedValueGraph.FiniteDecision.guardOfNoCycle _
    (GuardedValueGraph.FiniteDecision.noCycle_of_terminal (fun _ => rfl))

/-- The old request retains an old reference inside delayed argument code and
an independent bind/scope context outside its response continuation. -/
def saved : Saved (Fin 1) :=
  ⟨operation, .ref 0,
    .dynamicCall (.var 0) (.delay (.ret (.ref 0))),
    .bind (.scope 17 .hole) (.ret (.var 0))⟩

theorem saved_actual_request :
    CompTyped oldTypes emptyTy emptyContext saved.suspended unitTy :=
  .bind (.scope (.request (.ref 0)
    (.dynamicCall (.var rfl) (.delay (.ret (.ref 0)))))) (.ret (.var rfl))

theorem saved_capture : SavedTyped oldTypes saved unitTy :=
  capture_reached old_typed saved_actual_request (.refl _)

/-- A real source lambda and result consumer, with distinct binder scopes. -/
def callbackRhs : HigherOrder.Value :=
  .lambda .value receipt unitTy unitTy unitTy (.ret (.var 0))
    (.mk unitTy unitTy (.bind (.ret .unit) (.ret (.var 1))) [] [])
def callbackTypes : Fin 1 → Ty := fun _ => callableTy
def emptyCapture : Nat → Value (Fin 1) Empty := fun _ => .ref 0

theorem emptyCapture_typed : CapturesTyped oldTypes emptyContext emptyCapture := by
  intro i a h
  cases h

theorem callbackRhs_typed :
    HigherOrder.ValueTyped (sourceContext callbackTypes emptyContext) callbackRhs callableTy :=
  .lambdaValue (.ret (.var rfl)) (.mk (.bind (.ret .unit) (.ret (.var rfl))))

def freshOne := sourceFresh emptyCapture (fun _ : Fin 1 => callbackRhs)
abbrev First := Sum (Fin 1) (Fin 1)
def first : Graph First := allocate old freshOne
def firstTypes : First → Ty := joinTy oldTypes callbackTypes

theorem freshOne_equation (i : Fin 1) : freshOne i =
    .lambda .value receipt unitTy unitTy unitTy (.ret (.var 0))
      (.mk unitTy unitTy (.bind (.ret .unit) (.ret (.var 1))) [] []) := rfl

theorem freshOne_noCycle : FreshNoCycle freshOne :=
  GuardedValueGraph.FiniteDecision.noCycle_of_terminal (fun _ => rfl)

theorem first_typed : WellTyped first firstTypes :=
  allocate_typed old_typed freshOne
    (fun _ => sourceCloseValue_typed callbackRhs_typed emptyCapture_typed)

def firstGuard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph first) :=
  allocationGuard oldGuard freshOne freshOne_noCycle

def firstChain : Chain (Fin 1) old oldTypes First first firstTypes :=
  .snoc .refl (allocationEmbedding old oldTypes callbackTypes freshOne)

def identityAdapter {R : Type} : Adapter R Empty :=
  .mk unitTy unitTy (.ret (.var 0)) [] []
def responseOne : Value First Empty := .ref (.inr 0)
def responseTwo : Value First Empty := .wrap responseOne identityAdapter identityAdapter

theorem responseOne_typed : ValueTyped firstTypes emptyTy emptyContext responseOne callableTy := .ref _
theorem responseTwo_typed : ValueTyped firstTypes emptyTy emptyContext responseTwo callableTy :=
  .wrap responseOne_typed (.mk (.ret (.var rfl))) (.mk (.ret (.var rfl)))
theorem responses_distinct : responseOne ≠ responseTwo := by intro h; cases h

/-- Actual fresh lookup and lambda entry carry the real code and consumer. -/
def carrier : Value First Empty := .delay (.ret (.ref (.inl 0)))
def callbackPlan : LambdaEntryPlan First :=
  ⟨.value, receipt, unitTy, unitTy, unitTy, .ret (.var 0),
    .mk unitTy unitTy (.bind (.ret .unit) (.ret (.var 1))) [] [], carrier⟩
def afterEntry : Comp First Empty :=
  .bind (.scope 17 callbackPlan.computation) (.ret (.var 0))

theorem fresh_response_entry :
    Steps first ((saved.map Sum.inl).resume responseOne)
      [.lookup (.inr 0), .lambdaEntry callbackPlan] afterEntry :=
  .cons (.bind (.scope .callRef))
    (.cons (.bind (.scope .callLambda)) (.refl _))

theorem two_responses_safe
    (one : Steps first ((saved.map Sum.inl).resume responseOne) t1 n1)
    (two : Steps first ((saved.map Sum.inl).resume responseTwo) t2 n2) :
    (CompTyped firstTypes emptyTy emptyContext n1 unitTy ∧ CanProgress (graph := first) n1) ∧
    (CompTyped firstTypes emptyTy emptyContext n2 unitTy ∧ CanProgress (graph := first) n2) :=
  repeated_responses firstChain saved_actual_request first_typed firstGuard
    responseOne responseTwo responseOne_typed responseTwo_typed one two

/-- A SECOND source allocation captures the first graph's actual callback under
new delayed code. No old reference is overwritten and the new reference cannot
be typed in oldTypes or firstTypes. -/
def delayedTypes : Fin 1 → Ty := fun _ => .thunk callableTy
def callbackContext : Context := extend emptyContext callableTy
def callbackCapture : Nat → Value First Empty := fun _ => responseOne
def delayedRhs : HigherOrder.Value := .delay (.ret (.var 1))

theorem callbackCapture_typed : CapturesTyped firstTypes callbackContext callbackCapture := by
  intro i a hi
  cases i with
  | zero =>
      change some callableTy = some a at hi
      cases hi
      exact responseOne_typed
  | succ i => cases hi

theorem delayedRhs_typed :
    HigherOrder.ValueTyped (sourceContext delayedTypes callbackContext) delayedRhs (.thunk callableTy) :=
  .delay (.ret (.var rfl))

def freshTwo := sourceFresh callbackCapture (fun _ : Fin 1 => delayedRhs)
abbrev Second := Sum First (Fin 1)
def second : Graph Second := allocate first freshTwo
def secondTypes : Second → Ty := joinTy firstTypes delayedTypes

theorem freshTwo_equation (i : Fin 1) :
    freshTwo i = .delay (.ret (.ref (.inl (.inr 0)))) := rfl

theorem freshTwo_noCycle : FreshNoCycle freshTwo :=
  GuardedValueGraph.FiniteDecision.noCycle_of_terminal (fun _ => rfl)

theorem second_typed : WellTyped second secondTypes :=
  allocate_typed first_typed freshTwo
    (fun _ => sourceCloseValue_typed delayedRhs_typed callbackCapture_typed)

def secondGuard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph second) :=
  allocationGuard firstGuard freshTwo freshTwo_noCycle

def secondEmbedding : Embedding first firstTypes second secondTypes :=
  allocationEmbedding first firstTypes delayedTypes freshTwo

def secondChain : Chain (Fin 1) old oldTypes Second second secondTypes :=
  .snoc firstChain secondEmbedding

/-- This callable response mentions the brand-new delayed node in its BODY.
The computation-mode parameter remains a thunk, and the result consumer is real. -/
def secondResponse : Value Second Empty :=
  .lambda .computation receipt unitTy unitTy unitTy
    (.bind (.force (.ref (.inr 0))) (.dynamicCall (.var 0) (.var 1)))
    identityAdapter

theorem secondResponse_typed :
    ValueTyped secondTypes emptyTy emptyContext secondResponse callableTy :=
  .lambdaComputation
    (.bind (.force (.ref _)) (.dynamicCall (.var rfl) (.var rfl)))
    (.mk (.ret (.var rfl)))

theorem old_after_second_safe
    (steps : Steps second ((saved.map secondChain.embedding.refs).resume secondResponse) trace last) :
    CompTyped secondTypes emptyTy emptyContext last unitTy ∧ CanProgress (graph := second) last :=
  chain_resume_safety secondChain saved_actual_request second_typed secondGuard
    secondResponse secondResponse_typed steps

/-- One concrete interaction publishes the original request, extends, and
answers it using a newly allocated callable. -/
theorem first_interaction :
    Run (Fin 1) old oldTypes saved.suspended First first firstTypes
      ((saved.map Sum.inl).resume responseOne) [saved.map Sum.inl] := by
  apply Run.answer (saved := saved.map Sum.inl)
  · exact .extension (allocationEmbedding old oldTypes callbackTypes freshOne)
      (.publish saved .start) first_typed
  · exact List.mem_cons.mpr (.inl rfl)
  · exact .matched operation rfl responseOne
  · exact responseOne_typed

/-- The same stored record survives the first answer and a second allocation.
Its second answer uses code containing the newest delayed reference. -/
theorem second_interaction :
    Run (Fin 1) old oldTypes saved.suspended Second second secondTypes
      ((saved.map secondChain.embedding.refs).resume secondResponse)
      [saved.map secondChain.embedding.refs] := by
  apply Run.answer (saved := saved.map secondChain.embedding.refs)
  · have prior := Run.extension secondEmbedding first_interaction second_typed
    simpa only [List.map_cons, List.map_nil, saved_map_comp, secondChain,
      firstChain, Chain.embedding, Embedding.trans, Embedding.refl, allocationEmbedding, id] using prior
  · exact List.mem_cons.mpr (.inl rfl)
  · exact .matched operation rfl secondResponse
  · exact secondResponse_typed

/-- A second old saved request accepts a genuinely delayed fresh reference,
then forces and calls the returned callback in the old response continuation. -/
def delayedSaved : Saved (Fin 1) :=
  ⟨delayedOperation, .ref 0,
    .bind (.force (.var 0)) (.dynamicCall (.var 0) (.delay (.ret (.ref 0)))),
    .scope 19 .hole⟩

theorem delayedSaved_actual_request :
    CompTyped oldTypes emptyTy emptyContext delayedSaved.suspended unitTy :=
  .scope (.request (.ref 0)
    (.bind (.force (.var rfl)) (.dynamicCall (.var rfl) (.delay (.ret (.ref 0))))))

def delayedResponse : Value Second Empty := .ref (.inr 0)

theorem delayedResponse_typed :
    ValueTyped secondTypes emptyTy emptyContext delayedResponse (.thunk callableTy) := .ref _

theorem delayed_old_after_second_safe
    (steps : Steps second ((delayedSaved.map secondChain.embedding.refs).resume delayedResponse) trace last) :
    CompTyped secondTypes emptyTy emptyContext last unitTy ∧ CanProgress (graph := second) last :=
  chain_resume_safety secondChain delayedSaved_actual_request second_typed secondGuard
    delayedResponse delayedResponse_typed steps

/-- Same ID and endpoints, different ordered type arguments: still rejected. -/
def wrongInstance : OperationInstance := ⟨73, [], unitTy, callableTy⟩
theorem wrongInstance_distinct : wrongInstance ≠ operation := by
  intro h
  have args := congrArg OperationInstance.typeArguments h
  cases args

theorem wrongInstance_cannot_resume :
    ¬ Answer (saved.map Sum.inl) wrongInstance responseOne next :=
  mismatched_instance_rejected wrongInstance_distinct

/-- The exact old node equations also exclude replacement by a fresh lambda. -/
theorem overwrite_unit_rejected (e : Embedding old oldTypes first firstTypes)
    (bad : first (e.refs 0) = freshOne 0) : False := by
  have equation := e.nodes 0
  rw [bad] at equation
  change freshOne 0 = .unit at equation
  rw [freshOne_equation] at equation
  cases equation

end Demo
end YulangClosure.HigherOrderGraph.Extension

# Actual saved graph continuations under immutable extension

Status: candidate research mathematics, author checks NOT_RUN, independent review
NOT_RUN. No reviewed-theorem, source/native, implementation or production closure.
Author: `/root/graph_continuation_extension_astra_r1`; requested
`gpt-6-astra/medium`, observed model/effort UNKNOWN. No contributing descendants. Primary supplied
pre-freeze reserved-token/comment syntax feedback; this is not independent review.
Frozen authority: HANDLER-GRAPH-EXTENSION-THEORY-20261025/r1, outcome B,
contract SHA256 `b0b9f069dc8f08ed5f87a26b37d98df404e5a9dd4f0628244adc79095634a9e8`.
Baseline supplied by primary: `7ff6e74d4515099bdb13e1cbf20fc38257cb2e36`.

## Original claim and application

The paper at `docs/yulang-operational-type-safety-ja.tex:1139` quantifies over
arbitrary finite internal transitions, typed external responses with fresh
immutable graph nodes, and repeated uses of saved continuations. Its extension
lemma at line980 preserves old node values and types. The candidate supplies this
extension/response component for the **entire accepted HigherOrderGraph grammar**.
It does not claim the paper's omitted grammar, combined handler/graph language,
metadata adequacy, source/native correspondence, or Simple-sub A/B closure.

`GraphExtensionTransport.lean` maps references in arbitrary `Value R S`,
`Comp R S`, and `Adapter R S` to the same syntax with reference sort T and
unchanged recursive-name sort S. It retains recursive names, local indices,
full operation instances, literal contents, receipts, view occurrences, paths,
mode and type annotations. Unary both retains two distinct typing derivations.
Wrap keeps all independently quantified inner/input/output types. Lambda body
and outer consumer, adapter input, bind/union arm, and request response binders
retain their original scopes. Structural identity/composition, arbitrary local
renaming/substitution commutation, and typing are mutual constructor inductions.
The Empty specialization equals the accepted allocation `mapOld` structurally.

`Embedding` consists solely of an injective reference function, old type
equations, and actual old **node syntax** equations. Execution/observation/safety
is not an extension premise. Composition retains exact old nodes under composed
maps. `allocationEmbedding` consumes the actual accepted `allocate` constructor.
`map_step` and `map_steps` transport every raw graph step/event, including actual
lambda/wrap entry plan computations, lookup events, views, and finite traces.
Evaluation contexts and their plugging equations are transported explicitly.
Old-node overwrite and reference collision contradict the relation.

`GraphContinuationExtension.lean` stores the actual full operation instance,
payload, response continuation, and finite outer evaluation context in `Saved`.
`capture_typed` derives the existential continuation result type, payload type,
response binder and outer context typing from `Safety.request_context_typing`.
`capture_reached` first consumes actual internal Steps and preservation;
`capture_decomposition` consumes actual Requested decomposition. No saved typing
oracle is required by the parent application. `Saved.map` preserves complete
record syntax. `saved_map_resume` is a concrete substitution/plugging equation.

The dependent `Chain` allows arbitrary finite sequences of heterogeneous
reference sorts. `Chain.embedding`, `chain_old_nodes` and `chain_injective`
retain the composed injection and exact old content. `chain_resume_safety`
types each independently quantified response in the FINAL graph, then proves
all finite internal prefixes safe. It never requires a fresh reference to type
in the original graph. Final graph WellTyped/Guarded are explicit environmental
premises; typing alone does not imply a transparent-spine guard.
`repeated_responses` keeps two independent responses/traces/results;
`finite_response_family` gives every finite family, including the empty family.
`saved_after_second` identifies the original record after a second extension
syntactically. `chain_resume_four` obtains actual return, context request,
context failure, or next raw step.

`Run` makes the parent application an induction over arbitrary finite
**interleavings**: actual internal Step; actual request publication; immutable
extension of current computation and every stored record; and a matching typed
response to any stored record. Publication stores the original record, and
response does not remove it. The initial arena is empty. `run_invariant` derives
all arena typing from publication and preserves it under extension/reuse;
`run_prefix_safety` derives the original overall result type and four-way
progress after every final internal prefix when the final graph is Guarded.
This is an external research protocol, not a new native scheduler claim or a
replacement for raw Step. It tracks membership rather than native stable handles.
Its response constructor is the environmental typed-response contract; internal
rules contain no typing premises. Full operation equality is explicit in Answer.

## Actual allocations and discriminating applications

`source_allocation_resume` consumes actual source RHS derivations, independently
typed old captures, and `FreshNoCycle`. Existing `sourceCloseValue_typed`,
`allocate_typed` and `allocationGuard` supply new graph typing and guard. The
same derivation is used concretely in Demo's two successive finite allocations:

1. `callbackRhs` is a source value-entry lambda with real body `ret (var 0)`
   and a distinct result consumer `bind (ret unit) (ret (var 1))`. The fresh
   graph node is obtained through `sourceFresh`, with its exact syntax equation.
   The old saved request has an old reference in its delayed argument and an
   independent scope/bind outer context. `fresh_response_entry` constructs the
   actual lookup and lambda-entry prefix carrying this code and consumer.
2. `responseOne` is the fresh callable reference; `responseTwo` wraps that
   reference in typed input/output adapters. They are syntactically distinct.
   `two_responses_safe` applies the quantified theorem to both independent
   response executions of the same saved record.
3. A second source allocation creates delayed code that captures the first
   graph's callable. `secondResponse` is a computation-entry lambda whose body
   forces the newest reference and calls the resulting callback; its parameter
   remains a thunk and its consumer remains explicit. `old_after_second_safe`
   reuses the ORIGINAL saved request with this response. `first_interaction`
   and `second_interaction` exhibit actual publication/first answer/second
   extension/second answer in Run, retaining the original stored record.
4. `delayedSaved` is another original request with response type thunk(callable).
   Its old continuation forces that response and calls the callback.
   `delayed_old_after_second_safe` responds with the second allocation's actual
   delayed reference. Both graph typing and guards are derived from source RHS
   and finite allocation suppliers, not passed as example-specific oracles.
5. `wrongInstance` keeps operation ID and endpoint types but changes ordered
   type arguments. Full-instance Answer rejects it. `overwrite_unit_rejected`
   contradicts replacing an old unit node with the allocated lambda. The general
   collision theorem retains reference distinctness under arbitrary embeddings.

These are source-to-accepted-research-grammar constructions. They are not evidence
that native Rust constructors emit these logical graphs. The finite examples
supplement universal statements; they do not replace any quantifier.

## Native source audit and NO_SAFE_CODE_SLICE

Read actual frozen owners, without running or modifying native code:

| Owner | Actual behavior | Exact unresolved bridge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `machine.rs:2500` `begin_local`, `machine.rs:1498` `Frame::Local` | A local starts as a new `None` cell, recursive environment exposes its address, initializer completion assigns a `ReceivedValue`. | Define the logical graph domain and publication boundary. Show committed captured graph nodes retain their meaning; an initializing None-to-Some cell is not automatically an immutable logical graph extension. Sequential source initialization is not the simultaneous accepted source allocation theorem. |
| `machine.rs:2318` `stop_unhandled_request`, `machine.rs:350` `SavedContinuation` | Stores actual suffix, optional template, resumed flag and observations; a template is generated only on the selected host-write route. | Connect actual payload/full declaration/suffix to Saved's whole context and response binder, plus typing and graph/environment interpretation. |
| `continuation.rs:13` `ResumeTemplate`, `TemplateNode`; `machine.rs:1913` `enter_template` | Immutable template nodes contain frames/environment handles. Replay resolves active owners, may freshen invocations, reinstalls forwarded handlers and reobserves views. | Preserve full operation instance and graph references through current environment/cell reads, control remapping, receipt/view replay and error paths. These are not supplied by structural mapContext. |
| `machine.rs:600` `resume_host_write` | Checks stopped state/handle/operation/declaration/payload and rejects a saved record already marked resumed. | This host endpoint has an explicit one-use restriction. It is not an implementation of the general repeated-resume protocol proved here. No bug verdict or removal of the restriction follows. |
| `machine.rs:2081` `propagate_request` | Examines the live installed handler delimiter and actual source operation information before forwarding. | The accepted graph machine suspends under contexts. Native forwarding and current handler eligibility require their own correspondence and live metadata proofs. |

**NO_SAFE_CODE_SLICE**: graph projection/publication, complete request capture,
current native value/code/consumer readback, and live owner/view replay remain
unproved. No dependent compiler/runtime edit is authorized or inferred from this
candidate. Minimal provisional TODO requests are below; they request evidence,
not permissions or changes to the native contract.

## Reuse, exclusions, and remaining premises

Reused only within actual accepted premises: HigherOrderGraph's complete syntax
and local substitution; source split/closure and finite fresh-cycle allocation;
canonical observation/progress, actual request-context inversion, and finite
internal trace preservation. The new generic reference map has its own
constructor proofs; allocation's old map is connected by explicit equations.
The accepted HandlerInteraction protocol is conceptual prior work only, not an
import or a source of graph correspondence. No new lane-A module is imported.
Historical literal readback does not cover callable/delayed responses; native

excluded failed module or conditional premise is used as an unconditional fact.

Full-paper recursive/nominal/type-changing roll, polymorphism, records/constructors,

and OPEN at their existing owners. Combined handler/graph integration requires

# Higher-order research core and structural embedding

Status: Draft research construction; checking and review evidence is recorded in
the sprint outcome and its frozen receipts. This is not production authority.
Scope: frozen LEAN-HIGHER-ORDER-PROOF-CORE-20261025/r1 research representation.
Initial author: /root/higher_order_proof_core_astra_r1; requested gpt-6-astra/medium,
observed model/effort UNKNOWN. Primary /root repairs and integrates after author
STOP; the outcome records final authorship and independent review. No descendants.
Production authority: none. The operational paper is a proposal/target; the
2026-10-07 complete-Call definition §1 records permission for legitimate research
definitions, not adoption of this representation as compiler architecture.

The parent RESPONSE-ENCODING-1 / ENV-CALLABLE-1 lacked a callable constructor in
its formal Value sort. The candidate removes that specific representational
obstruction by constructing a new callable type and actual lambda/wrap values.
Every Original.Val/Comp and TypedCall.Value/Comp/Adapter/Function constructor is
mapped structurally. No old term is retained behind an opaque original opcode.
The full parent, native readback and operational safety remain OPEN.

## Syntax and quantifiers

`HigherOrderSyntax.lean` retains every old type constructor, all eight literal
domains and their exact payload representations, variables, delay, injections,
single-child intersection/top values and all seven Original computations. It
adds the existing Call view/scope/expose/request/fail nodes, lambda/wrap values,
and dynamicCall. Request's continuation binds its operation instance's response
type. The type language can place callable types beneath thunk/union/intersection
and in operation instances. The value, computation and adapter syntax is mutually
inductive; all typing judgments are defined afterwards.

Value-entry lambda binds A; computation-entry lambda binds Thunk A. Both retain
receipt, annotated input/body/result types, body and result consumer. Wrap keeps
the input adapter c→a and output adapter b→d around an a→b function. DynamicCall
accepts a thunk carrier. This fixes a research typing interface without asserting
an execution rule or operational equivalence for the new constructor.

`ContextEmbedding old new` quantifies over every old lookup fact. The mutual
Original and TypedCall preservation proofs quantify over arbitrary old terms,
old typing derivations and target contexts satisfying that relation. Closed
Original nodes embed under any target context using the empty lookup relation;
binders use `extend_embedding`. The Function theorem quantifies over every old
FunctionTyped derivation and every target context. No original constructor,
source-domain restriction or independent continuation quantifier is discarded.
This is one-way typing preservation, not reflection or full conservativity.

## Metadata boundary

Paths retain component lists, port kinds and translated endpoint types;
occurrences retain identities and paths. Operation instances retain operation
identity, ordered type arguments and both payload/response types. Receipt slots
and profiles retain order, identity and typed paths. Adapter metadata retains
all path correspondences and captured occurrences. Interface-port metadata also
has a structural map.

PathRule is a Prop in the accepted input. `embedPathRule` translates its proof
into a new Prop proof. It does not eliminate that proof into a data-valued map
identity. In particular the old permissive adapterMap rule remains permissive;
this work cannot prove that a mappingIdentity absent from runtime data can be
reconstructed. Syntax is **typing-proof-free**, not entirely proof-free. The old
Adapter.typed field is omitted from syntax and consumed solely to construct the
new extrinsic AdapterTyped derivation. The retained PathRule metadata neither
contains a typing judgment nor creates a typing-definition cycle.

## Parent application

`embedFunction_typed` constructs a ValueTyped callable from an old FunctionTyped
proof. `function_as_argument` and `call_with_function_argument` use it in the
actual new delayed argument and dynamicCall constructors.
`request_callable_response` constructs a request that binds and returns a
callable-typed response. `function_cell` pushes the embedded function into the
existing generic NativeClosureEnvironment.Store, proves the actual current cell
equality and supplies its callable typing derivation.

`read_embedding` preserves the exact old selected cell address while mapping the
current store pointwise. `read_embedding_typed` combines that equation with the
accepted `successful_read_typed` theorem. `captured_value_typed` applies the
accepted `realized_substitution_typed` supplier to each represented context index;
`captured_body_typed` applies its actual successful capture and closed-body
construction before embedding. Both keep successful realization and CellsTyped
as explicit original premises. Nothing claims that arbitrary native closures
already satisfy those premises, or that old stores already represent new
callable values. Generic new callable storage and old represented-read transport
are two separate constructions whose native connection is still open.

## Remaining source obligations and reuse

Accepted CoreSyntax typing and CallEnvironmentRealization supply precisely their
existing domains. CoreSubstitution's bind/request lifting is reused through
close_body, without reproving lookup or assuming a new substitution rule. The
NativeClosureEnvironment.Store remains generic; no machine fields change.
Historical literal readback is not extended to callable readback by analogy.
No failure is dismissed by a narrower theorem; no new source restriction,
Simple-sub bypass or production implementation is introduced.

Luna/source intake owns ENV-LAYOUT-1 (resolved free-variable order and binder
indices from source Lambda/Name/Apply), ENV-CELL-VALUE-1 (current native Value
encoding), ENV-GRAPH-1 (recursive cell/closure graphs), ENV-CALLABLE-1's remaining
native body/consumer mapping, and ENV-DISPATCH-1. Relevant native owners remain
machine.rs `Instruction::Lambda`, `Frame::ValueEntry`, `Machine::lookup`,
`Machine::extend`, closure/Callee branches and receiving.rs lambda schema
construction. The primary's disjoint source map gives their complete exact
producer/consumer inventory, including unit/record/default entry cases.
Force, native transitions, new-core substitution/progress/preservation,
whole-trace safety, operation authenticity and original inference A/B remain
OPEN. No F1/FK1 or foreign-continuation theorem is claimed here.

## Intake and checks

No Lean/build/tests/native checks were run by the author. A shell `python`
invocation failed because the executable was absent; the generation was then
performed with python3. This was a file-writing failure before any write, not a
failed proof check. Primary owns bounded elaboration, public signature/axiom
inspection, distinguishing examples, repairs after author STOP and fresh
independent review. Author/coauthor cannot independently certify this candidate.
Only the four exact leased files were created; there are no scratch paths,
background processes, descendants, compiler changes or Git operations.

# Combined higher-order handlers and guarded value graphs

Status: candidate research construction, pending primary elaboration and fresh
independent review. Production authority: none. Parent:
`HO-HANDLER-GRAPH-COMPOSITION-1`, paper guarded values 180–196, recursive
allocation 980–993, shallow handlers 399–456, local preservation 1069–1088,
and safety 1139–1159. The original paper theorem and Simple-sub A/B, F1/FK1
quantifiers remain OPEN.

Contract: `HANDLER-GRAPH-EXTENSION-THEORY-20261025/r1`, SHA-256
`b0b9f069dc8f08ed5f87a26b37d98df404e5a9dd4f0628244adc79095634a9e8`.
Author: `/root/handler_graph_composition_astra_r1`; primary `/root` supplied the
wait-result reference coverage reminder and cancellation-hypothesis shadowing
repair observation. Neither is eligible to independently certify this packet.
Requested model/effort: `gpt-6-astra/medium`; observed model/effort: UNKNOWN.
No descendants, additional dependencies, scratch paths, compiler changes or
production semantic decisions.

## Original claim and candidate application

The parent needs one actual syntax and execution relation supporting both
accepted languages simultaneously. Separate safety theorems were insufficient:
the old graph machine suspends requests/failures inside finite evaluation
contexts, while the old handler machine propagates them to the root. The new
candidate constructs the shared grammar, derives finite observations from the
actual graph typing and guard, and proves preservation and root-only progress
for every finite raw internal prefix. It then connects both old machines and
consumes the actual old recursive allocation supplier under an independently
typed combined handler.

`HandlerGraphSyntax` has six mutually recursive sorts: Value, Comp, Adapter,
Handler, ValueArms and OperationArms. Every accepted Graph and Handler
constructor is represented structurally. References, recursive names and local
indices remain distinct. Lambda bodies, outer result consumers, adapter input
bodies, request response binders, value-arm binders and both operation-arm
binders contain the full combined language. The existing Ty, modes, operation
instances, literal payloads and all metadata fields are reused unchanged.
Extrinsic typing and structural renaming/substitution cover every constructor.
The six cancellation lemmas justify substitution after binder insertion; they
are applied to the actual context resumption equation.

`HandlerGraphEmbedding` recursively embeds both old languages in arbitrary
typing contexts. Its renaming/substitution commutation lemmas are consumed by
actual old-step simulation. `liftGraph_typed` derives new node typing from old
node derivations. `liftGraph_projection` proves exact equality of the guard
projections, so `liftGraph_guard` transports the existing guard. Projected unit
is only a stopping token; it supplies neither typing nor a canonical value.

`HandlerGraphSafety` derives `ObservedTyped` from actual node typing and the
transparent successor rank. Intersection has two separate premises, top retains
its underlying type witness, and wrap retains different inner and outer callable
types and both adapters. No typing premise occurs in `Step`. Lookup is explicit
for force, union/intersection elimination, absurd and dynamic call, and also for
references returned as No/Yes carriers inside both kinds of wait. The machine
retains all shallow-handler trial, ordering, skipping, nesting, propagation and
restoration rules. The selected arm receives the original K:Q→A; only exhaustion
constructs the shifted handler around K, yielding H K:Q→B. Eligibility remains
raw Bool data, with no native permission adequacy claim. `preservation` assumes
actual closed graph typing; `closed_progress` additionally consumes the guard.
`finite_prefix_safety` quantifies over every raw finite internal trace.

`HandlerGraphCorrespondence.graph_step` and `handler_step` map every old raw
step, actual event and complete lambda/wrap entry plan. Their finite trace
versions preserve event order. `propagate_graph_request` and
`propagate_graph_failure` construct finite sequences through every old context;
`graph_suspended_root` consumes the old full suspension decomposition.
`graph_request_correspondence` retains the identical full operation instance and
payload and derives the resulting continuation typing from the old contextual
computation typing plus actual propagation. `graph_resume_equation` states that
substituting any combined response into the propagated continuation equals the
same outer context around the original response-substituted K.
`old_graph_resume_equation` further identifies this with the embedding of the
old resumed contextual computation. `graph_resumption_safety` applies the
supplier to arbitrary independently typed responses and every subsequent
internal prefix, without consuming the saved code or imposing linear use.

`source_rec_under_handler` calls the exact accepted `source_rec_allocation`,
lifts its actual allocated graph and closed body, derives combined typing and
guard, and establishes every finite prefix under an independently typed combined
handler. Its only fresh guard premise is the old actual `FreshNoCycle`; no new
fresh-node typing or rank supplier is introduced. `SourceExample` starts with
an empty old graph, closes a genuinely recursive source lambda with a request
and self-call in the response continuation, gives the exact allocated-node
equation, and executes its request through handler selection. `Examples` also
executes a recursive graph lambda through a graph-backed attempt/wait result,
and a nested request followed by restoration, reference lookup and Yes return.
The examples supplement the quantified statements.

## Reused evidence and exact open boundaries

The accepted Handler syntax/substitution/trial construction and Graph
syntax/allocation/observation construction are reused within their actual finite
constructor domains. Their independent safety conclusions were not assumed to
compose. The previous contextual graph terminal convention is not reused as
combined root progress. Literal readback, template replay, closure environments
and historical Call proofs are not treated as universal higher-order native
readback or metadata suppliers. No failed or withdrawn Simple-sub bypass is
restored. No residual, provider, witness or foreign-continuation lineage is
identified by this construction.

The original paper remains OPEN for omitted μ/type-changing roll,
polymorphism, mapop, primitive and other forms. This packet does not allocate
arbitrary new combined handler-valued RHS simultaneously: it embeds the actual
accepted old RHS allocation and permits independently typed combined handlers
around its body. Combined external responses carrying fresh graph extensions
remain a future integration with the independent extension lane; no cross-lane
import is assumed. Live metadata, grants, activation/owner freshening and full
source/native correspondence remain OPEN. The internal safety candidate does
not imply F1, FK1, inference soundness/principality or production adoption.

## Source/native audit and mutual TODOs

`tools/inference-playground/src/runtime/machine.rs` was inspected at these
actual owners:

- `begin_local` (2500) allocates an empty cell, extends recursive environments
  before evaluating the initializer, and pushes `Frame::Local`. The return
  branch (1498) installs the received value into that cell. The proof's immutable
  finite graph allocation is not an established readback of every such native
  execution or arbitrary initializer.

# Actual saved graph continuations under immutable extension

Status: candidate research mathematics, author checks NOT_RUN, independent review
NOT_RUN. No reviewed-theorem, source/native, implementation or production closure.
Author: `/root/graph_continuation_extension_astra_r1`; requested
`gpt-6-astra/medium`, observed model/effort UNKNOWN. No contributing descendants. Primary supplied
pre-freeze reserved-token/comment syntax feedback; this is not independent review.
Frozen authority: HANDLER-GRAPH-EXTENSION-THEORY-20261025/r1, outcome B,
contract SHA256 `b0b9f069dc8f08ed5f87a26b37d98df404e5a9dd4f0628244adc79095634a9e8`.
Baseline supplied by primary: `7ff6e74d4515099bdb13e1cbf20fc38257cb2e36`.

## Original claim and application

The paper at `docs/yulang-operational-type-safety-ja.tex:1139` quantifies over
arbitrary finite internal transitions, typed external responses with fresh
immutable graph nodes, and repeated uses of saved continuations. Its extension
lemma at line980 preserves old node values and types. The candidate supplies this
extension/response component for the **entire accepted HigherOrderGraph grammar**.
It does not claim the paper's omitted grammar, combined handler/graph language,
metadata adequacy, source/native correspondence, or Simple-sub A/B closure.

`GraphExtensionTransport.lean` maps references in arbitrary `Value R S`,
`Comp R S`, and `Adapter R S` to the same syntax with reference sort T and
unchanged recursive-name sort S. It retains recursive names, local indices,
full operation instances, literal contents, receipts, view occurrences, paths,
mode and type annotations. Unary both retains two distinct typing derivations.
Wrap keeps all independently quantified inner/input/output types. Lambda body
and outer consumer, adapter input, bind/union arm, and request response binders
retain their original scopes. Structural identity/composition, arbitrary local
renaming/substitution commutation, and typing are mutual constructor inductions.
The Empty specialization equals the accepted allocation `mapOld` structurally.

`Embedding` consists solely of an injective reference function, old type
equations, and actual old **node syntax** equations. Execution/observation/safety
is not an extension premise. Composition retains exact old nodes under composed
maps. `allocationEmbedding` consumes the actual accepted `allocate` constructor.
`map_step` and `map_steps` transport every raw graph step/event, including actual
lambda/wrap entry plan computations, lookup events, views, and finite traces.
Evaluation contexts and their plugging equations are transported explicitly.
Old-node overwrite and reference collision contradict the relation.

`GraphContinuationExtension.lean` stores the actual full operation instance,
payload, response continuation, and finite outer evaluation context in `Saved`.
`capture_typed` derives the existential continuation result type, payload type,
response binder and outer context typing from `Safety.request_context_typing`.
`capture_reached` first consumes actual internal Steps and preservation;
`capture_decomposition` consumes actual Requested decomposition. No saved typing
oracle is required by the parent application. `Saved.map` preserves complete
record syntax. `saved_map_resume` is a concrete substitution/plugging equation.

The dependent `Chain` allows arbitrary finite sequences of heterogeneous
reference sorts. `Chain.embedding`, `chain_old_nodes` and `chain_injective`
retain the composed injection and exact old content. `chain_resume_safety`
types each independently quantified response in the FINAL graph, then proves
all finite internal prefixes safe. It never requires a fresh reference to type
in the original graph. Final graph WellTyped/Guarded are explicit environmental
premises; typing alone does not imply a transparent-spine guard.
`repeated_responses` keeps two independent responses/traces/results;
`finite_response_family` gives every finite family, including the empty family.
`saved_after_second` identifies the original record after a second extension
syntactically. `chain_resume_four` obtains actual return, context request,
context failure, or next raw step.

`Run` makes the parent application an induction over arbitrary finite
**interleavings**: actual internal Step; actual request publication; immutable
extension of current computation and every stored record; and a matching typed
response to any stored record. Publication stores the original record, and
response does not remove it. The initial arena is empty. `run_invariant` derives
all arena typing from publication and preserves it under extension/reuse;
`run_prefix_safety` derives the original overall result type and four-way
progress after every final internal prefix when the final graph is Guarded.
This is an external research protocol, not a new native scheduler claim or a
replacement for raw Step. It tracks membership rather than native stable handles.
Its response constructor is the environmental typed-response contract; internal
rules contain no typing premises. Full operation equality is explicit in Answer.

## Actual allocations and discriminating applications

`source_allocation_resume` consumes actual source RHS derivations, independently
typed old captures, and `FreshNoCycle`. Existing `sourceCloseValue_typed`,
`allocate_typed` and `allocationGuard` supply new graph typing and guard. The
same derivation is used concretely in Demo's two successive finite allocations:

1. `callbackRhs` is a source value-entry lambda with real body `ret (var 0)`
   and a distinct result consumer `bind (ret unit) (ret (var 1))`. The fresh
   graph node is obtained through `sourceFresh`, with its exact syntax equation.
   The old saved request has an old reference in its delayed argument and an
   independent scope/bind outer context. `fresh_response_entry` constructs the
   actual lookup and lambda-entry prefix carrying this code and consumer.
2. `responseOne` is the fresh callable reference; `responseTwo` wraps that
   reference in typed input/output adapters. They are syntactically distinct.
   `two_responses_safe` applies the quantified theorem to both independent
   response executions of the same saved record.
3. A second source allocation creates delayed code that captures the first
   graph's callable. `secondResponse` is a computation-entry lambda whose body
   forces the newest reference and calls the resulting callback; its parameter
   remains a thunk and its consumer remains explicit. `old_after_second_safe`
   reuses the ORIGINAL saved request with this response. `first_interaction`
   and `second_interaction` exhibit actual publication/first answer/second
   extension/second answer in Run, retaining the original stored record.
4. `delayedSaved` is another original request with response type thunk(callable).
   Its old continuation forces that response and calls the callback.
   `delayed_old_after_second_safe` responds with the second allocation's actual
   delayed reference. Both graph typing and guards are derived from source RHS
   and finite allocation suppliers, not passed as example-specific oracles.
5. `wrongInstance` keeps operation ID and endpoint types but changes ordered
   type arguments. Full-instance Answer rejects it. `overwrite_unit_rejected`
   contradicts replacing an old unit node with the allocated lambda. The general
   collision theorem retains reference distinctness under arbitrary embeddings.

These are source-to-accepted-research-grammar constructions. They are not evidence
that native Rust constructors emit these logical graphs. The finite examples
supplement universal statements; they do not replace any quantifier.

Show committed captured graph nodes retain their meaning; an initializing None-to-Some cell is not automatically an immutable logical graph extension. Sequential source initialization is not the simultaneous accepted source allocation theorem. |

Replay resolves active owners, may freshen invocations, reinstalls forwarded handlers and reobserves views. | Preserve full operation instance and graph references through current environment/cell reads, control remapping, receipt/view replay and error paths. These are not supplied by structural mapContext. |

It is not an implementation of the general repeated-resume protocol proved here. No bug verdict or removal of the restriction follows. |
| `machine.rs:2081` `propagate_request` | Examines the live installed handler delimiter and actual source operation information before forwarding. | The accepted graph machine suspends under contexts. Native forwarding and current handler eligibility require their own correspondence and live metadata proofs. |

**NO_SAFE_CODE_SLICE**: graph projection/publication, complete request capture,
current native value/code/consumer readback, and live owner/view replay remain
unproved. No dependent compiler/runtime edit is authorized or inferred from this
candidate. Minimal provisional TODO requests are below; they request evidence,
not permissions or changes to the native contract.

## Reuse, exclusions, and remaining premises

Reused only within actual accepted premises: HigherOrderGraph's complete syntax
and local substitution; source split/closure and finite fresh-cycle allocation;
canonical observation/progress, actual request-context inversion, and finite
internal trace preservation. The new generic reference map has its own
constructor proofs; allocation's old map is connected by explicit equations.
The accepted HandlerInteraction protocol is conceptual prior work only, not an
import or a source of graph correspondence. No new lane-A module is imported.
Historical literal readback does not cover callable/delayed responses; native
